## 14.10 Theorem 10.13: The Two-Sphere First-Contact Collision as the Physical Selection Event

**McGucken Principle anchor.** Under dx₄/dt = ic, every spacetime event is the apex of its own McGucken Sphere expanding at +ic (Definition 4.1 property (d) of §4). A measurement is an event at which two such Spheres — the emitter's Sphere from source event p_E and an absorber's Sphere from a candidate detector-electron event p_A — meet for the first time at a single spacetime point. That first-contact event is the physical selection event: it identifies which one absorber, out of the ensemble of candidates, registers the detection. Selection is a geometric fact about two expanding null hypersurfaces meeting first at exactly one place before they meet anywhere else.

The 3-slice projection reading of §14.2 (Theorem 10.1) and the Sphere-surface dilution reading of §38a.4 (Theorem 28.5a below) together answer *why the un-realized alternatives are gone* — the projection restricts Ψ(x, x₄) to the constant-x₄ slice through the measurement event, and the +ic-monotonic surface dilution |ψ|² ∝ 1/A(t) renders the alternative configurations irrecoverable. Neither reading answers *what physically constitutes the pointlike registration event* by which one collision, at one absorber, is realized on a given trial. The present theorem supplies that answer at the level the geometry supplies: the registration event is a first-contact collision between the emitter's Sphere and one absorber's Sphere, giving the definiteness of the outcome (one pointlike collision per trial, one absorber realized) and, through the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure, the Born distribution over which absorber is realized across many trials. The identity of the specific realized absorber on a specific trial remains as the determinism-vs-chance seed the framework leaves open, at the fork every framework reaches; the geometry does not supply it. Decoherence removes the off-diagonals; the two-Sphere first-contact collision supplies the pointlike physical registration event and the Born distribution; the 3-slice projection is that event's algebraic shadow on the observer's constant-x₄ hypersurface; Sphere-surface dilution renders the un-realized alternatives irrecoverable. Four geometric facts, all descending from dx₄/dt = ic, plus the stated open seed at the determinism-vs-chance fork, giving the full measurement account.

**Theorem 10.13 (Two-Sphere First-Contact Collision, Grade 2; consolidates [12, §28.8.10.4] — the head-on-Sphere-collision mechanism at lines 12100–12140 of the source paper — together with [238, §XI.5-bis] (the definiteness-plus-distribution-plus-open-seed trichotomy in the measurement paper), [238, §V.5-bis] (the closed detector-sphere worked example), and [237, Theorem 7.7] (detection-event reading of ψ*); rests on Definition 4.1 (every event is a Sphere apex) and Theorem 3 property (c) (+ic monotonicity)).** *Let ρ_E denote the state emitted at event p_E and let {p_A^(k)} denote the ensemble of candidate absorber events (detector-electron events) in the causal future of p_E. Let Σ₊(p_E) denote the emitter's McGucken Sphere and Σ₊(p_A^(k)) denote each candidate absorber's Sphere. On any single trial, the measurement registration event is a pointlike spacetime event P* at which Σ₊(p_E) and Σ₊(p_A^(k*)) collide for some k* from the ensemble — the two Spheres meeting at P* in a first-contact head-on encounter with antiparallel x₄-orientations. The geometry supplies (a) the definiteness of the outcome — exactly one such collision physically occurs on each trial, at one pointlike event, involving one absorber from the ensemble; and (b) the distribution over which absorber k* is the one involved — the Born distribution |ψ(P)|² derived through the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure (Step 4 below). The three-spatial localization of the emitted quantum at P* is supplied by the antiparallel x₄-orientations of the two colliding Spheres at P*, per the head-on-collision mechanism of [12, §28.8.10.4]. The identity of the specific k* on a specific trial — the "which absorber this time" question — is the determinism-vs-chance seed the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework leaves open, at the fork every framework reaches.*

**Proof.** Four steps.

*Step 1 (Universal Sphere content).* By Definition 4.1 property (d), every spacetime event is the apex of its own McGucken Sphere. In particular, the emitter event p_E sources Σ₊(p_E) expanding at +ic from p_E, and every candidate absorber event p_A^(k) sources Σ₊(p_A^(k)) expanding at +ic from p_A^(k). Each Sphere is the null hypersurface of x₄-advance from its apex (Theorem 2.5 of §4.1).

*Step 2 (First-contact collision as pointlike registration event).* Consider the intersection Σ₊(p_E) ∩ Σ₊(p_A^(k)) for each candidate k. Each such intersection, when non-empty, contains a first spacetime event — the event with the smallest coordinate-time value on which both Spheres coincide. Call this event P^(k). On any single trial, exactly one of these first-contact events is physically realized: one collision P* = P^(k*) occurs at one pointlike spacetime event, involving one absorber k* from the ensemble. The geometry supplies the definiteness — one collision, one pointlike event, one absorber realized per trial. Which candidate absorber is the one realized on a given trial is the per-trial seed the framework leaves at the determinism-vs-chance fork; across trials, the distribution over which candidate is realized is the Born distribution derived through the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure of Step 4 below.

*Step 3 (Antiparallel x₄-orientation at P*).* At the first-contact event P*, both Σ₊(p_E) and Σ₊(p_A^(k*)) are outgoing null hypersurfaces from their respective apices. The emitter's Sphere has outgoing x₄-orientation +ic at P* in the emitter's rest frame. The absorber's Sphere, having propagated from p_A^(k*) toward the emitter's spatial location, presents its outgoing wavefront direction at P* as pointing back toward the emitter — that is, viewed in the emitter's rest frame, the absorber Sphere's local x₄-orientation at P* reads −ic along the shared spatial geodesic through P*. The relative-frame reading of the two Spheres' orientations at P* is therefore antiparallel: (+ic) and (−ic). This is the head-on-collision content of [12, §28.8.10.4], reproduced here in the measurement setting.

*Step 4 (Spatial localization at P*).* By conservation of four-content across the four dimensions of the McGucken manifold, the antiparallel x₄-content at P* — the (+ic) + (−ic) = 0 net x₄-orientation along the shared spatial geodesic — is balanced by the appearance of both particles at the same spatial three-slice location at P*. The x₄-content that cancelled at P* is deposited as spatial three-slice localization of the emitted quantum at P*: the detector click. The localization rate is bilinear in the two Sphere amplitudes,

$$\text{Rate}_{\text{collision}}(P) \propto \phi^*(P)\,\psi(P),$$

where ψ(P) is the amplitude for Σ₊(p_E) to reach P and φ(P) is the amplitude for Σ₊(p_A^(k*)) to reach P, with the complex conjugate on the absorber amplitude being the frame-relational reading of the absorber's outgoing +ic as incoming −ic in the emitter's frame at P. Summed over absorber final states with the appropriate matrix elements, the rate reduces to the Born rule form |ψ(P)|², recovering the Born probability density at the collision event ([12, §28.8.10.4] eqs. 12122–12124). The physical realization of one pointlike outcome — one first-contact collision at one absorber, per trial — is the geometric content of the head-on-collision mechanism; the distribution over which absorber is realized across many trials is the Born distribution derived here; the identity of the specific k* on a specific trial is the per-trial seed the framework leaves open, at the determinism-vs-chance fork every framework reaches. ∎

**Relation to decoherence, projection, and dilution.**

- *Decoherence.* Removes the off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix (Zurek 2003; §14.9 above). - *Sphere-surface dilution (Theorem 28.5a of §38a.4).* Renders the un-realized candidate configurations irrecoverable via |ψ|² ∝ 1/A(t) as the emitter Sphere continues to expand past P*. The four are complementary. Decoherence supplies the preferred basis; first-contact collision supplies the pointlike physical registration (one collision per trial) and, through the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure, the Born distribution over which absorber is realized across many trials; 3-slice projection is the algebraic shadow of the realized registration; Sphere-surface dilution renders the un-realized alternatives irrecoverable. The per-trial identity of which absorber realizes the collision is the seed the framework leaves at the determinism-vs-chance fork every framework reaches.

## 14.10a Theorem 10.14: The PT-Symmetry-Through-Source-Event Reading of ψ*

**McGucken Principle anchor.** Under dx₄/dt = ic, the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p_E) is spherically symmetric about its source event p_E. The natural symmetry of that Sphere through p_E is the combined parity-and-time-reversal operation PT_E sending (x − x_E, t − t_E) ↦ −(x − x_E, t − t_E) in the four-dimensional geometry. This 4D PT_E-reflection is an exact symmetry of the McGucken-Sphere expansion at every event, supplying a physical meaning for the complex conjugate ψ* of a freely propagating wavefunction that does not require any absorber to be present.

Theorem 10.13 of §14.10 above supplies ψ* the detection-event reading — the absorber's forward +ic-expansion seen antiparallel in the emitter's frame at the head-on-collision point (imported from [12, §28.8.10.4] and [237, Theorem 7.7]). That reading requires an absorber. A freely propagating particle before it interacts with any detector has a well-defined ψ and a well-defined |ψ|² carrying probability content, yet no absorber Sphere is present. The present theorem supplies the second reading, applicable to free propagation.

**Theorem 10.14 (PT-Symmetry Through the Source Event, Grade 2; consolidates [237, Theorem 7.11] and [238, §III.1-ter]).** *Let ψ(x, t) denote the wavefunction of a freely propagating quantum with source event p_E = (x_E, t_E). Let PT_E denote the four-dimensional parity-and-time-reversal operation through p_E, sending (x − x_E, t − t_E) ↦ −(x − x_E, t − t_E). Then the wavefunction satisfies the identity*

$$\psi(PT_E \cdot \text{event}) = \psi^*(\text{event})$$

*exactly (Fourier-decomposed over plane-wave components with their explicit PT_E transformation). Complex conjugation of ψ is therefore identified geometrically as the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event: the Born density at any event P is the product ψ(P, t) · ψ(2x_E − P, 2t_E − t), the value of the wavefunction at the PT_E-reflected event. The ψ* factor has a physical referent — the wavefunction at the PT_E-reflected event of the same forward-expanding Sphere — even in the absence of any absorber.*

**Proof.** For a plane-wave component ψ_k(P, t) = exp(i k · (P − x_E) − i ω(k)(t − t_E)), the 4D PT_E-reflection sends both the spatial phase k · (P − x_E) ↦ −k · (P − x_E) and the temporal phase ω(k)(t − t_E) ↦ −ω(k)(t − t_E), giving

$$\psi_k(PT_E \cdot (P, t)) = \exp(-i k \cdot (P - x_E) + i \omega(k)(t - t_E)) = \psi_k^*(P, t).$$

The identity holds on each plane-wave component; by linearity of Fourier decomposition it holds on any wavefunction expressible as a superposition of plane waves ([237, Theorem 7.11]). The bilinear pairing ψ*(P, t) ψ(P, t) that produces the Born density is therefore the product of ψ at the field event with ψ at its PT_E-reflected event; the two factors are two values of one wavefunction on one Sphere, related by the Sphere's own PT symmetry. No backward-in-time wave is invoked — every McGucken Sphere expands forward at +ic; PT_E is a symmetry of the geometry, not a dynamical rule. ∎

**Distinction from the antipodal-at-fixed-t map.** An earlier framing of the free-propagation reading identified complex conjugation with the antipodal map P ↦ 2x_E − P on the 2-sphere at fixed parameter time t. This antipodal-at-fixed-t map reverses the spatial phase k · (P − x_E) ↦ −k · (P − x_E) but leaves the temporal phase ω(k)(t − t_E) unchanged, so it yields complex conjugation only up to a residual temporal-phase factor exp(−2i ω_k (t − t_E)) that vanishes only for energy eigenstates. For general non-stationary wavefunctions the residual factor does not vanish. The exact statement is therefore the full 4D PT_E symmetry of Theorem 10.14, not the spatial-slice antipodal map.

**The two readings together.** Theorem 10.13 (detection-event reading) and Theorem 10.14 (free-propagation reading) place the complex conjugate factor ψ* on the same geometric foundation as the complex character of ψ itself. The complex structure of ψ comes from i as the perpendicularity marker of x₄ (Statement 2.1 of §2); the conjugation of ψ* comes from the reversal of x₄-orientation — the absorber's Sphere seen antiparallel in the detection-event reading (Theorem 10.13), the PT_E-reflection through the source event in the free-propagation reading (Theorem 10.14). Both are reversals of the forward +ic-advance relative to a reference: relative to the emitter's frame in the first case, relative to the source event p_E in the second. Neither invokes a backward-in-time wave. The bilinearity ψ*ψ that the rank-2 Minkowski metric forces from Lemma 7.1 of [237] is thereby given its complete physical content: the two factors are the forward x₄-expansion and its orientation-reversed reading, meeting at the event where the Born density is evaluated, with the reversal supplied by an absorber Sphere in the interaction regime and by the source-event PT symmetry in the free-propagation regime.

**Consequence for the "wavefront persists" reading.** The free-propagation reading supports a physical consequence noted at [238, §V.5-ter closing paragraph]: the nonlocal wavefront of x₄'s expansion may persist beyond the measured particle. The first-contact collision (Theorem 10.13) localizes the particle out of the expansion at a single spacetime event; the x₄-expansion itself — the ongoing advance of the fourth dimension carrying its own PT_E-symmetric structure through every event — continues after the particle has been registered. The particle rode the expanding surface while it was in flight; the detection collision transferred the particle's momenergy into the absorber's localized state; the underlying dx₄/dt = ic expansion persists at every spacetime event as it always did. The measurement observed the nonlocal properties of x₄ through the particle's interaction with an absorber; the expansion itself is not consumed by the observation.

# 15. The Twelve Arrows of Time and Their Subsidiary Asymmetries

Beyond the canonical five, the literature recognizes additional asymmetries:

(f) The *electromagnetic* arrow — the radiation reaction is dissipative.
(g) The *gravitational-wave* arrow — gravitational radiation propagates outward.
(h) The *CP-violation* arrow — the kaon system shows weak-interaction time-asymmetry (Christenson, Cronin, Fitch, Turlay 1964).
(i) The *neutrino-flavor* arrow — neutrino oscillations show CP-violating asymmetries.
(j) The *biological-evolution* arrow — sequence-information accumulates forward in time (Wallace 2013).
(k) The *cognitive* arrow — predictive coding works forward, not backward.
(l) The *baryogenesis* arrow — the Sakharov 1967 conditions for matter-antimatter asymmetry require time-asymmetric processes.

All twelve descend from x₄'s +ic monotonicity. Arrows (f) and (g) are radiative-arrow (Theorem 8) projections in the electromagnetic and gravitational sectors. Arrows (h) and (i) are the CP-violation content of [43] traced to the +ic orientation of weak-interaction Lagrangian terms. Arrows (j) and (k) are biological-arrow projections (Theorem 9). Arrow (l) is the baryogenesis projection — Sakharov's three conditions require time-asymmetry, and the time-asymmetry is the +ic of x₄. Each subsidiary arrow has its own theorem in the source corpus; we mention them to establish that the derivational unification is not limited to the canonical five.

**Tier placement of the subsidiary arrows.** Within the Two-Tier Architecture (Theorem 10.5 of §14.7), the seven subsidiary arrows distribute across the derivational tiers as follows. Arrows (f), (h), (i), and (l) — the electromagnetic, CP-violation, neutrino-flavor, and baryogenesis arrows — are Tier 1 matter-dynamics arrows specialized to specific Lagrangian sectors (electromagnetic Maxwell sector; weak-interaction Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa sector; baryogenesis Sakharov-three-conditions sector). Each is a Tier 1 projection of the matter-dynamics signature-pair (thermodynamic Euclidean / quantum-measurement Lorentzian) into a specific physical interaction. Arrows (j) and (k) — the biological-evolution and cognitive arrows — are Tier 1 subordinates, derived from the thermodynamic arrow (Theorem 9) plus the radiative arrow (Theorem 8) acting on biological and neural information substrates. Arrow (g) — the gravitational-wave arrow — sits between Tier 1 and Tier 2: gravitational radiation propagates on the McGucken manifold (Tier 1 propagation) but is sourced by mass-energy distributions whose dynamics drive Tier 2 metric response. In each case, the +ic orientation of the subsidiary arrow traces to the same Tier 0 +ic of dx₄/dt = ic that sources the canonical five.

The derivational picture is therefore the following. All twelve arrows descend from one Tier 0 principle. The matter-dynamics arrows form a Wick-rotation signature-pair at Tier 1 with the canonical thermodynamic (Euclidean) and quantum-measurement (Lorentzian) arrows as the two readings of one process. The cosmological arrow lives at Tier 2 as the metric's own arrow. The seven subsidiary arrows are sector-specific Tier 1 (or Tier 1 / Tier 2 transitional, for the gravitational-wave case) projections of the same +ic content. The derivational unification is uniform: one principle, three tiers, twelve arrows.



# PART III — THE CLASSICAL PARADOXES DISSOLVED

# 16. Theorem 11: Loschmidt's 1876 Reversibility Objection Derivationally Dissolved

**Theorem 11 (Dissolution of Loschmidt's Reversibility Objection, Grade 2, consolidates [12, Th. 12]).** *Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection — that time-symmetric microscopic Newtonian dynamics cannot rigorously force a time-asymmetric Second Law — is derivationally dissolved in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. The time-symmetric microscopic dynamics descend from the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel; the time-asymmetric Second Law descends from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel. The two channels are dual readings of one principle, not competing foundations.*

**Proof.** Boltzmann 1872 derived the H-theorem dH/dt ≤ 0 from the Stosszahlansatz applied to molecular collisions. Loschmidt 1876 observed: the underlying Newtonian dynamics are time-reversal symmetric, so for every entropy-increasing trajectory there exists by velocity reversal a corresponding entropy-decreasing trajectory of equal statistical weight. The Stosszahlansatz — assumption of pre-collision molecular chaos — is itself the time-asymmetric content the argument is supposed to derive; the argument is therefore circular.

The McGucken-framework dissolution proceeds in three steps:

*Step 1 (the Algebraic Channel is time-symmetric).* The algebraic-symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic includes temporal uniformity, spatial homogeneity, spherical isotropy, Lorentz covariance, and absence of preferred phase origin on x₄. These symmetries generate Noether conservation laws (energy from temporal uniformity, momentum from spatial homogeneity, angular momentum from spherical isotropy, etc.) ([19]). The Noether currents are time-symmetric quantities: each conservation law is symmetric under time reversal. The time-symmetric microscopic dynamics of Newtonian and Hamiltonian mechanics are the Algebraic Channel output.

*Step 2 (the Geometric Channel is time-asymmetric).* The geometric-propagation content of dx₄/dt = ic includes spherical expansion at rate c from every event, monotonic radial growth of the McGucken Sphere, isotropic wavefront emission, and one-way advance at +ic. These geometric features are intrinsically time-asymmetric: the McGucken Sphere expands monotonically and one-way. The time-asymmetric Second Law dS/dt > 0 (Theorem 6) and the five arrows of time (Theorem 5) are the Geometric Channel output.

*Step 3 (The two channels coexist by Klein 1872).* By the Klein correspondence (Theorem 4), the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel are not independent foundations but the algebra-side and the geometry-side of one Kleinian object. The same principle dx₄/dt = ic carries both time-symmetric and time-asymmetric content because algebra and geometry are the two information-equivalent descriptions of the same object.

Loschmidt's objection assumed that time-symmetric content and time-asymmetric content must come from different foundations, and hence cannot coexist in a coherent theory. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework demonstrates that the assumption is wrong: a single principle can carry both, in two distinct channels, and the dual-channel structure is the resolution. The time-symmetric Newtonian dynamics that Loschmidt invoked are correct as the Algebraic Channel. The time-asymmetric Second Law that Boltzmann tried to derive from those dynamics is correct as the Geometric Channel. The standard derivation that smuggles in the Stosszahlansatz fails because it tries to derive the Geometric Channel from the Algebraic Channel alone — an impossibility, since the Algebraic Channel's output is time-symmetric. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework resolves the issue by recognizing that the Geometric Channel is independent of the Algebraic Channel and is the source of the time-asymmetric content. Both descend from the same single principle dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

**Comparison with standard treatments.** Boltzmann 1877 retreated to a statistical answer — that entropy-decreasing trajectories are vanishingly rare — surrendering the derivation. Reichenbach 1956 and Albert 2000 located the asymmetry in the Past Hypothesis. Carroll 2010 catalogued the unsatisfactoriness. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the derivational dissolution: the Second Law does not derive from the time-symmetric Algebraic Channel (an impossibility), but from the time-asymmetric Geometric Channel of the same principle (a derivational necessity).

## 16.1 Corollary 11.1: The Two-Atom Emission–Absorption as the +ic Orientation Exhibited Below Thermodynamics

**McGucken Principle anchor.** Under dx₄/dt = ic, the +ic orientation is a property of the principle at every event, exhibited in every process at every scale — not only in statistical-mechanical ensembles. A single emission event and a single absorption event, involving two individual atoms, exhibit the +ic-monotonic advance of x₄ directly at the level of one two-atom process, without requiring any ensemble average, coarse-graining, or thermodynamic-limit statement. The retarded (not advanced) Green's-function selection at the single-event scale is the +ic monotonicity read at the microscopic level.

The current corollary imports the two-atom double-slit derivation of [236, §XI.3.11] into the present paper as the direct sharpening of Theorem 11. That source transcribes the companion paper [235] and the flagship [237, §10.12septies]. The full transcription — thirteen numbered theorems, propositions, and corollaries with their proofs, plus the comparison table and the answer to Maudlin's three measurement problems — is given verbatim in §16.1a below. Corollary 11.1 states the umbrella result; §16.1a supplies the full derivation. Where Theorem 11 dissolves Loschmidt's reversibility objection by identifying the Second Law as the Geometric Channel content of dx₄/dt = ic, Corollary 11.1 (with §16.1a) exhibits the +ic orientation below the level at which thermodynamics operates: in a single two-atom emission–absorption event, the retarded (forward-in-time) Green's function is selected over the advanced (backward-in-time) Green's function as a direct geometric consequence of dx₄/dt = ic, without any statistical-mechanical intermediary.

**Corollary 11.1 (Two-Atom Emission–Absorption as +ic-Oriented Below Thermodynamics, Grade 2; consolidates [236, §XI.3.11] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies], with the full theorem chain in §16.1a below; rests on Theorem 3 property (c) (+ic monotonicity) and Theorem 8 of §12 (radiative arrow / Green's-function decomposition)).** *Let atom A at event p_E emit a single quantum (photon or other massless boson) that propagates to atom B at event p_A > p_E in the causal future of p_E. The emission event p_E is at coordinate time t_E; the absorption event p_A is at coordinate time t_A > t_E; the +ic-monotonic advance of x₄ between p_E and p_A is a geometric fact about the two-atom process, exhibited at the level of one emission and one absorption, without requiring any thermodynamic or ensemble content.*

*Formally: the retarded Green's function G_ret(p_A; p_E) supports the propagator between the two events, and the advanced Green's function G_adv(p_A; p_E) does not appear in the physical process. The selection is forced by dx₄/dt = ic's +ic orientation at both p_E and p_A. The two-atom process therefore exhibits the primitive time orientation — the +ic of the principle itself — at the smallest scale accessible to any physical interaction, one full Compton-cycle below the level at which any thermodynamic average could be defined.*

**Proof.** Four steps.

*Step 1 (Retarded Green's function support).* By Theorem 8.0 of §12.1, the retarded Green's function of the wave equation is supported on the forward null cone (McGucken Sphere) of the source event: G_ret(x, t; x', t') = δ(t - t' - |x - x'|/c)/(4π|x - x'|) with support on t > t'. Applied to the emission event p_E, the retarded Green's function propagates from p_E along Σ₊(p_E) (Definition 4.1) at rate c toward events in the causal future of p_E.

*Step 2 (Absorption event on the emitter's forward null cone).* The absorption event p_A at atom B lies on Σ₊(p_E), the McGucken Sphere from the emission event. The emitted quantum reaches p_A along a null worldline of Σ₊(p_E), with the absorption event's coordinate time t_A satisfying t_A - t_E = |x_B - x_A|/c where x_A, x_B are the spatial positions of the two atoms in the common inertial frame. The two-atom process is the physical realization of one null worldline of Σ₊(p_E) — the specific null geodesic connecting p_E to p_A.

*Step 3 (Advanced Green's function absent).* The advanced Green's function G_adv(x, t; x', t') = δ(t - t' + |x - x'|/c)/(4π|x - x'|) would support propagation from p_E along Σ₋(p_E), the backward null cone from p_E. By Theorem 3 property (c) of §6, no McGucken Sphere Σ₋ expands at −ic; the principle dx₄/dt = ic admits +ic only, and the geometric ensemble at every event is Σ₊ only. The advanced Green's function has no physical realization as a McGucken-Sphere propagation, so the two-atom process is exclusively retarded: G_ret contributes, G_adv does not.

*Step 4 (Below-thermodynamics scale).* The two-atom emission–absorption process involves exactly two atoms — the emitter and the absorber. No ensemble average is taken. No coarse-graining is performed. No thermodynamic limit is invoked. The +ic-monotonic advance of x₄ between p_E and p_A is a geometric fact about the single two-atom process, exhibited at the scale of one Compton-cycle of the emitted quantum (or fewer, depending on the emission process). This scale is below the level at which any statistical-mechanical or thermodynamic quantity can be defined (both require multi-particle ensembles); the +ic orientation is exhibited at a scale where thermodynamic averaging does not yet operate. The primitive time orientation of the principle is therefore visible below thermodynamics. ∎

**Consequence for Jaimungal's time-symmetry challenge.** In the Curt Jaimungal / Al-Khalili *Ontology of Time* interview (October 2025), Jaimungal presses at 1:11:09: *"The statistical arguments you gave are time symmetric... entropy, if it's low at some time here, it actually will increase in the future, but also increase in the past... But then how do we know that we're evolving into the future or that this is the past, and the Big Bang is the future, and we're just switching the arrow?"* Al-Khalili concedes: *"Well, we don't."*

Corollary 11.1 answers Jaimungal's challenge directly: we know because the +ic orientation is exhibited at the single two-atom emission–absorption scale, below the level at which statistical-mechanical time-symmetry arguments even apply. Jaimungal's challenge assumes that the arrow of time enters physics only through statistical arguments about entropy, which are time-symmetric in their microscopic substrate. The two-atom emission–absorption process shows that this assumption is wrong: the +ic orientation is present in one two-atom event, not only in ensemble-averaged Second-Law content. The direction from p_E to p_A is +ic, not −ic; this is a geometric fact about the two-atom process, exhibited without any ensemble average, and it directly resolves Jaimungal's "how do we know."

Al-Khalili's fallback to Gold universes and mirror universes (which he acknowledges have "no empirical evidence") is unnecessary in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework: the primitive orientation is exhibited at every single two-atom event in every laboratory experiment ever performed on emission-absorption processes, so no cosmological-boundary stipulation is needed. Wheeler–Feynman's absorber is recovered as a derived consequence at the cosmological scale, but the primitive selection operates locally at every two-atom emission-absorption event.

**The two-scale empirical bracket: Corollary 11.1 paired with Theorem 10.6 (Brownian Hamlet).** The +ic monotonicity of dx₄/dt = ic is exhibited empirically across the full scale-range of physical processes, with two demonstrations serving as endpoints of the bracket. **Corollary 11.1 (the present subsection)** exhibits the +ic orientation at the minimal scale — a single emission event, a single absorption event, two atoms, no environment, no ensemble, no coarse-graining — one Compton-cycle below the level at which any thermodynamic quantity can be defined. ## 16.1a Full Transcription of [236, §XI.3.11]: The Two-Atom Double Slit — Thirteen Numbered Results and Maudlin's Three Problems Answered

The following subsection transcribes verbatim, with proper renumbering for the present paper, the full §XI.3.11 of [236] — *The McGucken Philosophy of Physics: Physics from One Principle, dx₄/dt = ic, Derives the Quantum Formalism, the Measurement Postulate, and the Arrow of Time from a Single Physical-Geometric Statement about Spacetime*. That section is itself a self-contained transcription of the companion paper [235] and the flagship [237, §10.12septies]. The theorems, propositions, corollaries, and equations are renumbered here to fit the present paper's scheme (11.1.1–11.1.13 for the numbered results; equations S.1–S.6 kept with the source's labels for cross-reference). Every result carries its source label in parentheses so any reader can trace the citation back to [236, §XI.3.11] or to [235] and [237, §10.12septies] directly.

**The thought experiment.** Take the double-slit experiment and remove everything removable: the room, the glass, the screen, the thermal bath, the detector electronics. What remains is a partition with two apertures, one atom A on side M, one atom B on side N, and one excitation. Atom A emits; the photon passes the partition; atom B absorbs. Run it the other way — atom B emits — and ask whether the photon retraces its path to A. Two readings must be separated: whether A ever absorbs, and whether the forward process is run backward. It reaches A with the forward interference weight (Theorem 11.1.5 below) and retraces the forward wave history with probability zero. The system is minimal by construction: two degrees of freedom and one field, no ensemble, no coarse-graining, no entropy count. Whatever irreversibility survives here is present before thermodynamics begins, and the conclusion is that it is the choice of the retarded solution of a time-symmetric field equation, a sign on the time coordinate, and that dx₄/dt = ic is the single statement from which that sign follows.

**Setup.** Let side M be the half-space z<0, side N the half-space z>0, and the partition the plane z=0 with aperture function T(x,y) = 1 on S₁ ∪ S₂ (the two slits) and 0 otherwise. Atom A sits at **r**_A with z_A<0; atom B at **r**_B with z_B>0. Work first with a scalar field for a monochromatic excitation, ψ(**r**,t) = U(**r**) e^{−iωt}, k=ω/c; the spatial part obeys the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation with the emitting atom as source,

$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\,U(\mathbf{r}) = -\delta(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_{\rm src}). \tag{S.1}$$

The analysis carries over verbatim to the vector Maxwell field and to the Schrödinger wave of a massive particle, each being time-reversal invariant in the sense of Theorem 11.1.1 with retarded and advanced Green's functions related as in (S.3). The barrier is reflecting in the first five theorems and absorbing in Theorem 11.1.7; the two cases differ, and the difference is part of the content.

**Theorem 11.1.1 of §16.1a (T-invariance; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Theorem 10.12S.1] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *The wave equation □ψ = −4πρ, the source-free Maxwell equations, and the Schrödinger equation with real potential are each invariant under time reversal: if ψ(**r**,t) is a solution, so is ψ(**r**,−t) (wave; Maxwell with **B** → −**B**) or ψ*(**r**,−t) (Schrödinger).*

*Proof.* For the wave equation ∂_t² is even in t. For Maxwell, the substitution t → −t, **E** → **E**, **B** → −**B**, **j** → −**j** maps the equations to themselves. For Schrödinger, complex conjugation of i∂_tψ = Hψ with H real gives −i∂_tψ* = Hψ*, the original equation in −t. ∎

This is standard (Jackson §6.10; Sakurai §4.4); it is stated because the rest turns on it — the equation does not orient time, so whatever orients time is added to it. The Helmholtz equation (S.1) has two Green's functions,

$$G_\pm(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}') = \frac{e^{\pm ik|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}'|}}{4\pi|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}'|}, \tag{S.2}$$

which with the time factor e^{−iωt} are the retarded (outgoing, G₊) and advanced (incoming, G₋) solutions, related by

$$G_-(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}') = G_+(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}')^*. \tag{S.3}$$

Both satisfy (S.1); the equation is indifferent between them. This is the Ritz–Einstein point of 1909.

**Proposition 11.1.2 of §16.1a (Forward amplitude; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Proposition 10.12S.2] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *Atom A emits the retarded solution U_A(**r**) = G₊(**r**,**r**_A). With a reflecting barrier, the field on side N is given by the Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integral over the aperture plane,*

$$U_A(\mathbf{r}_N) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\iint T(x,y)\,U_A(x,y,0^-)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{ikL_N}}{L_N}\right) dx\,dy, \qquad L_N = |\mathbf{r}_N - (x,y,0)|, \tag{S.4}$$

*and the probability that B absorbs is proportional to |U_A(**r**_B)|², the two-slit interference weight at **r**_B.*

*Proof.* Kirchhoff–Rayleigh–Sommerfeld diffraction for an aperture in a plane screen (Born and Wolf §8.3); the restriction to S₁ ∪ S₂ is the two-source coherence producing interference at **r**_B. ∎

Denote the forward field on all of side N by U_A|_N; it is an extended field determined on the entire half-space by the aperture data, and U_A(**r**_B) is one value of it.

**Theorem 11.1.3 of §16.1a (Exact reversal requires the advanced solution; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Theorem 10.12S.3] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *The time-reverse of the forward process is the solution U_A*. On side N it is the incoming, phase-conjugate field U_A*|_N, which converges through the apertures onto **r**_A; it is the advanced solution G₋(**r**,**r**_A) restricted to the two-slit geometry.*

*Proof.* Apply Theorem 11.1.1 to the forward solution: ψ_A(**r**,t) = U_A(**r**)e^{−iωt} maps to ψ_A(**r**,−t), spatial part U_A*(**r**); by (S.3), U_A* = G₋(·,**r**_A) filtered by T, incoming on **r**_A. ∎

**Theorem 11.1.4 of §16.1a (A point emitter produces the retarded solution; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Theorem 10.12S.4] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *Atom B re-emitting produces U_B(**r**) = G₊(**r**,**r**_B), the outgoing spherical wave centered on **r**_B, its restriction to the aperture plane z=0⁺ having phase fixed by the distance from **r**_B to each point of S₁ ∪ S₂.* Which of G_± describes emission is a property of the emitter, and it is the retarded one.

**Theorem 11.1.5 of §16.1a (Non-retracing; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Theorem 10.12S.5] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *With a reflecting barrier, the re-emission from B does not retrace the forward path. The field on side M is*

$$U_B(\mathbf{r}_M) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\iint T(x,y)\,U_B(x,y,0^+)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{ikL_M}}{L_M}\right)dx\,dy, \tag{S.5}$$

*an extended diffraction pattern over side M. The probability that A absorbs is proportional to |U_B(**r**_A)|², and by Helmholtz reciprocity U_B(**r**_A) = U_A(**r**_B), so the return probability equals the forward interference weight at B, which is strictly less than the total weight over side M.*

*Proof.* By Theorem 11.1.3, exact retracing requires the boundary data U_A*|_{z=0⁺}, the conjugate of the forward field, an extended converging wavefront. By Theorem 11.1.4, B supplies U_B|_{z=0⁺}, the restriction of an outgoing spherical wave. The two agree at no point in general; the overlap of U_B|_N with U_A*|_N is the single complex number ⟨U_A*, U_B⟩ ∝ U_A(**r**_B)*, one component of the continuum exact reversal requires. The remainder of U_B diffracts afresh through the apertures and spreads over side M by (S.5); reciprocity G₊(**r**_A,**r**_B) = G₊(**r**_B,**r**_A) gives the return amplitude. ∎

**Corollary 11.1.6 of §16.1a (The asymmetry is not geometric; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Corollary 10.12S.6] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *The map from the field on side M to the field on side N through a reflecting two-slit partition is unitary on the transmitted subspace and is inverted exactly by the conjugate boundary data of Theorem 11.1.3. The double-slit geometry therefore does not produce the irreversibility; its role is to spread the boundary data exact reversal requires over an extended aperture, so the mismatch between the required incoming wavefront and the outgoing wavefront a point atom supplies is visible at every point of the aperture plane.*

*Proof.* The reflecting barrier conserves the field norm; transmitted and reflected components are orthogonal projections. Phase conjugation of the transmitted field, propagated back, reconstructs U_A on side M (Theorem 11.1.3); this is realized experimentally by time-reversal mirrors (Fink 1992). ∎

The reading in which the partition "discards information" so that geometry alone forbids reversal is therefore wrong: with a reflecting barrier nothing is discarded, the blocked component returns into side M and remains in the system, and reversal fails for one reason only — the emitter is oriented.

Theorems 11.1.5 and 11.1.7 are independent: the first holds with a reflecting barrier and no absorption, the second with conjugate boundary data and no point-emitter restriction. Only the first survives when everything removable is removed, and it is the one the thought experiment isolates.

**Theorem 11.1.8 of §16.1a (Retarded selection is a sign choice; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Theorem 10.12S.10] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *The retarded and advanced Green's functions of the wave operator are the two boundary values of the same analytic function,*

$$\tilde G(\mathbf{k},\omega) = \frac{1}{k^2 - \omega^2/c^2}, \qquad G_{\rm ret} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega + i\varepsilon, \quad G_{\rm adv} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega - i\varepsilon, \tag{S.6}$$

*and the choice between them is the sign of the infinitesimal imaginary displacement of the frequency, equivalently the sign of the imaginary part of the time coordinate in the Fourier kernel e^{−iωt}.*

*Proof.* The poles of (S.6) at ω = ±ck are displaced into the lower half ω-plane by +iε, so the inverse transform vanishes for t<0 (retarded); the opposite displacement gives vanishing for t>0 (advanced). ∎

This is the exact location of the asymmetry: the equation is symmetric (Theorem 11.1.1), emission is oriented (Theorem 11.1.4), and the orientation is the sign in (S.6). Every account of irreversibility at the level of a single emission event must supply that sign, and the accounts differ in what they add to the field equation to supply it — Ritz (1908–1909) adds a rule, use G₊; Wheeler–Feynman (1945) adds a perfect-absorber boundary condition on the totality of absorbers; the standard thermodynamic account adds a low-entropy initial condition. None derives the sign from a prior kinematic fact about events.

Emission from a point atom is therefore outgoing as a consequence of the Principle.*

The +iε prescription of (S.6) is the infinitesimal form of that identification: displacing ω by +iε is equivalent to giving t a small imaginary part of sign fixed by the orientation of x₄-advance, and +ic fixes that orientation as +. With the displacement sign fixed, Theorem 11.1.8 yields G_{\rm ret}, and a point source then emits the outgoing wave G₊, which is Theorem 11.1.4. ∎

Both propositions hold, and they are compatible: unitarity is a property of the evolution operator between emission and absorption, while the realized process contains two further steps, the oriented emission (Theorem 11.1.4) and the localized absorption (Proposition 11.1.12), neither of which is an instance of the unitary operator. Two quantities present at the start of the reverse process are absent at its end: the extended field U_B|_M with its value at every point of side M (after A absorbs, those values are gone), and the advanced solution G₋ (of the two solutions the equation permits, one is realized and the other discarded before propagation begins). The two-atom system contains no environment into which to defer the projection: either the projection occurs and the field values on the rest of side M are lost, or the excitation remains spread over side M and A has not absorbed.

**Proposition 11.1.13 of §16.1a (The measured event is what exists; source: [236, §XI.3.11, Proposition 10.12S.19] transcribing [235] and [237, §10.12septies]; Grade 2).** *In the two-atom system the measurement is absorption at A. This is the minimal system in which the three components — unitary evolution, oriented emission, localized absorption — can be separated and named, and it exhibits the +ic orientation with two atoms, one partition, one excitation, and one measurement.

*What the two-atom result settles for Maudlin's three problems.* The section separates the two claims the word "unitary" ordinarily conflates (Propositions 11.1.11 and 11.1.12): the evolution operator between emission and absorption is unitary, while the realized process is not, because it brackets that operator with an oriented emission (only G_{\rm ret} is realized; G_{\rm adv} is discarded before propagation begins, Theorem 11.1.4 and Theorem 11.1.9) and a localized absorption (the extended field U_B|_M collapsing to one atom is a projection, not a norm-preserving map, Proposition 11.1.12). This is the framework's answer to each of Maudlin's three problems, in a system with no environment into which anything could be hidden:

- *Problem of outcomes.* The absorption is a definite localized event — the excitation ends on one atom, not smeared across side M (Proposition 11.1.12). Definite outcomes are secured not by denying (1.B) with a stipulated collapse law but by the projective character of absorption, which is what absorption physically is when an extended wavefront meets a localized absorber. The completeness that fails is the completeness of the 3D ψ; the four-dimensional state (which the projection reads at a cross-section, per [236, Proposition V.1]) is complete.

- *Problem of statistics.* The Born weight |U_A(**r**_B)|² is present already in the forward amplitude (Proposition 11.1.2) and is the SO(3)-Haar measure on the McGucken Sphere generated by the emission (Corollary 11.1.10; [236, Proposition III.1]) — derived, not stipulated, which is what Maudlin demands of a real solution. And the framework escapes Maudlin's Many-Worlds verdict precisely because it is single-world: there *is* something for the number |U_A(**r**_B)|² to be the probability of — namely, that the one excitation is absorbed at A rather than elsewhere on side M. The "nothing for the numbers to be probabilities of" objection that defeats the multiverse reading, and that Vedral's self-locating-uncertainty route cannot escape ([236, §XI.3.10]), does not touch a framework with one world and one absorption event.

- *Problem of effect.* The absorption physically localizes the excitation on B (forward) or on A (reverse); the post-absorption state carries that outcome forward, so a repeated measurement finds the excitation where the first absorption placed it. The framework passes the problem of effect the way Maudlin's surviving collapse theories do — the state-change at measurement propagates into the future — but without a separate collapse *law*: the projection *is* the absorption, not an added dynamical term. Modal interpretations fail Problem 3 because their additional variable carries no forward influence; the framework's absorption event is a real localization that does.

The framework therefore passes all three of Maudlin's problems, and it does so while adding none of the three things his taxonomy says a solution must add — no hidden variable on an intact linear wave, no non-linear collapse law, no branching worlds. It passes them by the two-atom demonstration that the realized process is not strictly unitary, so that (1.B)-as-universal is false and the trilemma does not bind. This is the sense in which the framework is new physics of the kind Maudlin requires — a stated primitive (dx₄/dt = ic), a specified primitive ontology (the McGucken Sphere and the absorption event), and stated dynamics (the oriented emission, the unitary propagation operator, the projective absorption) — rather than a reinterpretation of the existing formalism, which Maudlin rightly consigns to the flames.
